title: Joining Tables: INNER JOIN
description: Combine columns from two tables based on a related foreign key column.

blocks.content:
Relational databases store data across separate tables. `INNER JOIN` matches rows where the join condition is met in both tables:

```sql
SELECT orders.id, customers.name
FROM orders
JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.id;
```

A join connects tables using a shared fact, like matching each library loan to the student ID that borrowed it. An inner join keeps only matches found on both sides.

The matching columns need related values, not necessarily the same column name. A missing match is left out of an inner join.

blocks.prompt: Join `students` and `enrollments` to get `students.name` and `enrollments.course_name` for all enrolled students.
blocks.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE students (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE enrollments (student_id INTEGER, course_name TEXT);
blocks.seed_sql: INSERT INTO students VALUES (1, 'Alice'), (2, 'Bob'); INSERT INTO enrollments VALUES (1, 'Math'), (1, 'Science'), (2, 'History');
blocks.answer_sql: SELECT s.name, e.course_name FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON s.id = e.student_id;
